messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

{ "returncode": 0, "output_head": "# Chat Bots Design Notes ## Data Model (`User` + `User::Bot`) Bots are represented in the `users` table with `role: :bot` (`enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`): - **`creator_id`**: Foreign key to `users` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true`), recording which chat member created the bot. Because `User::Role#can_administer?` checks `administrator? || self == record&.creator`, creators and administrators automatically have permission to manage a bot while other regular members do not. - **`bot_token` & `bot_key`**: Active bots receive a unique 24-character `SecureRandom.base58` `bot_token` on creation. The externally visible bot code (`User#bot_key`) is `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`. `User.authenticate_bot(bot_key)` looks up the active bot by primary key `id` and compares `bot_token` in constant time via `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. - **Deactivation (Deletion)**: Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, and removes non-direct room memberships while preserving historical messages authored by the bot. - **Room Memberships**: Because bots are `User` records with `status: :active`, they automatically join all open rooms via `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` (and `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users`) and appear alongside human users in closed/direct room member selectors (`User.active`). Human-only flows (`/account/edit` member list, `/session`, session transfers, IP bans) scope queries with `User.without_bots`. ## Bot HTTP API (`Messages::ByBotsController`) - **Endpoint**: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`constraints: { room_id: /[^\/]+/, bot_key: /[^\/]+/ }`). - **Raw Body Handling**: `curl -d "..."` sends `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` by default even though the payload is raw text (which may contain `%`, `+`, `&`, etc.). `Messages::ByBotsController` sets `wrap_parameters false` and `request.request_parameters = {}` in `process_action` before Rails instrumentation accesses `request.filtered_parameters`, preventing Rack/Rails form/JSON parameter parsers from raising `400 Bad Request` on raw bodies. The raw UTF-8 body is read from `request.raw_post`. - **Validation & Extension Point for Attachments**: `Message` validates `ensure_body_or_attachment_present` (`body.blank? && body.body&.attachables.blank? && !attachment?`). If future features add file attachment uploads for bots (e.g., binary bodies by `Content-Type` or `multipart/form-data`), `Messages::ByBotsController#create` can attach the file and call `@message.process_attachment` before `@message.broadcast_create`. - **Broadcasts & Push Notifications**: Setting `Current.user = bot` sets `message.creator = bot`. Saving triggers `Room#receive` (`unread_memberships` + `Room::PushMessageJob`), and `@message.broadcast_create` appends the message via Turbo Streams and notifies `UnreadRoomsChannel`. ## Bot Webhooks (`Webhook` + `Webhook::DeliveryJob`) - **Data Model**: `Webhook` (`webhooks` table with `user_id` foreign key and `url`) belongs to `User` (`has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy, autosave: true` in `User::Bot`). `User::Bot` exposes `webhook_url` and `webhook_url=` so bot forms (`/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit`) can create, update, or clear a bot's webhook (saving an empty `webhook_url` destroys the `Webhook` record; `User#deactivate` also destroys it). - **URL Policy**: Validates `URI::HTTP` (`http`/`https`) with a present host, allowing self-hosted/internal/localhost endpoints without requiring external DNS resolution. - **@-Mention Autocomplete & Dispatch**: Active bots in a room appear in `Autocompletable::UsersController` alongside human members and use standard ActionText `User` attachables (`User::Mentionable`). On `Message` creation, `Room#receive` calls `deliver_webhooks_later`, which enqueues a `Webhook::DeliveryJob` (on the `default` queue) per active bot with a webhook in `message.mentionees` (ignoring bot-authored messages to prevent bot loops, and never blocking the HTTP request of the user posting the message). - **Payload & Stripped Command Text**: Posts `Content-Type: application/json` with `{ event: "mention", author, room: { id, name, reply_to }, message: { id, body: { text, html }, link } }`. `Message::Mentionee#plain_text_without_mention(bot)` strips only that bot's own `` nodes from the rich-text fragment while preserving other mentions and `message.body.html`. - **Synchronous vs. Asynchronous Replies**: - `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` escapes HTML entities and converts newlines to `
`, posting and broadcasting the message as the bot. - `200` with `Content-Type: text/html` posts and broadcasts rich-text HTML (sanitized by ActionText and `ContentFilters`) as the bot. - `204` (or non-text/non-200 responses) posts nothing synchronously; the bot can post asynchronously at any time via `room.reply_to` (`/rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`). ==", "output_tail": module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id
    has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy, autosave: true

    before_validation :sync_webhook, if: :webhook_url_assigned?
    validate :validate_webhook_url
    after_save :clear_assigned_webhook_url

    before_create :ensure_bot_token, if: :bot?

    validates :name, presence: true, if: :bot?

    scope :without_bots, -> { not_bot }
  end

  class_methods do
    def new_bot(attributes = {})
      bot.new(**attributes.to_h.symbolize_keys, creator: Current.user)
    end

    def create_bot!(attributes = {})
      new_bot(attributes).tap(&:save!)
    end

    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      bot_id, bot_token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil if bot_id.blank? || bot_token.blank?

      if user = active.bot.find_by(id: bot_id)
        user if user.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(user.bot_token, bot_token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  def webhook_url
    if webhook_url_assigned?
      @webhook_url
    elsif webhook && !webhook.destroyed? && !webhook.marked_for_destruction?
      webhook.url
    end
  end

  def webhook_url=(url)
    @webhook_url_assigned = true
    @webhook_url = url.to_s.strip.presence
  end

  def reload(...)
    clear_assigned_webhook_url
    super
  end

  private
    def webhook_url_assigned?
      @webhook_url_assigned == true
    end

    def clear_assigned_webhook_url
      @webhook_url_assigned = false
      @webhook_url = nil
    end

    def sync_webhook
      if @webhook_url.present?
        webhook.reload if webhook&.persisted? && webhook.marked_for_destruction?
        if webhook && !webhook.destroyed? && !webhook.marked_for_destruction?
          webhook.url = @webhook_url
        else
          build_webhook(url: @webhook_url)
        end
      else
        webhook&.mark_for_destruction
      end
    end

    def validate_webhook_url
      if webhook && !webhook.marked_for_destruction? && !webhook.valid?
        errors.add(:webhook_url, :invalid) if errors[:webhook_url].empty?
      end
    end

    def ensure_bot_token
      self.bot_token ||= generate_unique_bot_token
    end

    def generate_unique_bot_token
      loop do
        token = SecureRandom.base58(24)
        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
  end

  teardown do
    Current.reset
  end

  test "create_bot! creates an active bot owned by Current.user with a unique bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot")

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert bot.bot_token.present?
    assert_equal "#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}", bot.bot_key
    assert_includes users(:kevin).bots, bot
  end

  test "human users do not get a bot_token or bot_key" do
    user = User.create!(name: "Human", email_address: "human@example.com", password: "secret123456")

    assert user.member?
    assert_nil user.bot_token
    assert_nil user.bot_key
    assert_includes User.without_bots, user
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new_bot(name: "")
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "new bot automatically joins all open rooms" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot")

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
    assert_not_includes bot.rooms, rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "new open room grants access to existing active bots but not deactivated bots" do
    active_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Active Bot")
    deleted_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deleted Bot")
    deleted_bot.deactivate

    open_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Announcements", creator: users(:david))

    assert_includes open_room.users, active_bot
    assert_not_includes open_room.users, deleted_bot

**Deep Dive into Bot Membership Management**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. The core of this task revolves around giving bot authors granular control over which rooms their bots participate in, while still providing an option for global bot membership. I need to make sure I understand EVERY implication of the bot authors' requests.

The initial thought is to meticulously analyze *every* single requirement and interaction within the codebase. The prompt itself warrants a careful re-reading, sentence by sentence, ensuring I don't miss any nuances or constraints. QA automation's reliance on specific labels is a key point to remember; those quoted labels must be preserved exactly where the tests expect to find them, be it as visible text, a label, placeholder, or aria-label. The requirement for switches to be checkboxes, even if styled, along with the use of native `confirm()` dialogs is another critical aspect.

The bot author's requests are fundamental: bots should *not* automatically join all open rooms. They should have a *choice*. The second request highlights that even if they want their bot to serve everyone, they should *not* have to manually add the bot to each open room. Finally, the authors want to be notified (via a webhook) when their bot enters a new room.

The shift is clear: bots will no longer automatically join open rooms. Humans *will* continue to do so. The introduction of the "Add to all open rooms" switch on the bot form is the mechanism for global membership. This switch, when enabled, ensures the bot is a member of all existing and *future* open rooms. Turning it off preserves existing memberships, which is a key design consideration. The webhook `joined` event is crucial: it delivers a notification to the bot exactly once per room, which the bot can respond to in a way similar to a mention.

The next step is to analyze the existing code: in particular, the `Rooms::OpensController` and views. The `rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` snippet, along with the controller actions `new`, `create`, `edit` and `update` show how users were handled in the past, and how to allow the bots to now be added manually to a room. This is crucial for understanding the implications of the "no default join" change. Previously, all users, including bots, were implicitly members of all open rooms. No controls were present in `rooms/opens/_form.html.erb` for selecting individual users in an open room. The `Rooms::OpensController` actions ignored any potential `user_ids` parameter from the form, which is now important for understanding the next steps.

The critical question here is: how does a *person* manually add a bot to an *open* room? Given that open rooms were designed to be open by default, the interface for doing so is not immediately clear. Is there a workflow for manually adding *anyone* to an open room? Or did bots and people *always* enter automatically? This is key to ensuring that the UI meets the second user story of not having to add the bot to each open room. My immediate goal is to map out this possible flow, as the UI implications are not clear from the prompt. For example, if "Add to all open rooms" is off, how *does* a user explicitly add a bot to a room?

We're looking at rooms in Campfire. From the sidebar "+" leads to a new room, which is the `Rooms::OpensController#new` action. The settings button (...) on an open room leads to `Rooms::OpensController#edit` and the settings button (...) on a closed room leads to `Rooms::ClosedsController#edit`. 

Now, on the `Rooms::Open` routes (new and edit), we find the key control. There's an "Everyone" switch at the top, which toggles between open and closed rooms, changing the routes from `new_rooms_open_path` to `new_rooms_closed_path` or `edit_rooms_open_path(@room)` to `edit_rooms_closed_path(@room)`. We're going to keep this in mind as we read on.

Below "Everyone" is a list of users, `@users = User.active.ordered`. Previously, because `Rooms::Open` granted access to every active user, that's why `app/views/rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` displayed a simple checkmark next to every single user, using `check.svg`.
But hold on, let's compare the code for open and closed rooms (`app/views/rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` versus `app/views/rooms/closeds/_user.html.erb`).

In `app/views/rooms/closeds/_user.html.erb`, we see the user list with toggles to add or remove members (except for the current user and room owner/creator), which is exactly what we would expect in a closed room. Let's read the prompt again regarding Bot authors' needs: bots are added to open rooms via an on/off "add to all open rooms" switch on a bot form, and will receive a 'joined' event when added.

We need to look at both the HTML `<label>` and the `<input>` elements, which are key to understanding accessibility and test interaction. I need to make sure I understand the relationship between the `<label>` and `<input type="checkbox">` in HTML, especially how it works with our CSS.

The `inputs.css` file contains our styling for the switches and what’s important is how the styles affect interactions, particularly with the `checked` state, and the `:disabled` selectors. Now, to look at existing examples. We have existing switches in `accounts/edit.html.erb` and `rooms/closeds/_user.html.erb` that we can use as a reference.

Rails' `form.check_box` helper generates the checkbox and the hidden field. The critical part is the CSS selector `.switch__input:checked + .switch__btn`. We need the `.switch__btn` immediately after `.switch__input`, because the adjacent sibling combinator is key to our styling.

Let's not forget how `<label>` elements are associated with the checkbox.  If we have multiple labels pointing to the same checkbox, things can get weird, very quickly. We need to consider how the accessibility name is computed, and how that impacts Capybara and Playwright.  If you have two labels referencing the same input, that could lead to doubled accessible names, which would cause tests to fail.

Here, let's look at three options:

2.  Visible text is inside a `<label for="bot_auto_join_open_rooms">`. We then need a `<label class="switch">` wrapping the checkbox. We could work with that.

Looking at `inputs.css` again, it shows the `.switch` doesn't require being a `<label>`. This looks promising. If we can wrap the whole row in a `<label>`, the browser accessibility should naturally take care of it, and tests like Capybara and Playwright will easily find and interact with the element.

For Option C, let's verify:

1.  One `<label>` for the checkbox.
2.  The text visible *and* the accessible name will be identical, preventing duplication.

**Analyzing Bot Membership and Open Room Behavior**

Okay, taking a look at these code snippets, the UI design for the bot form is clean and consistent with the account edit page. The use of the same CSS classes for the "Add to all open rooms" switch as the admin-only switch in the account edit page is a nice touch. The `<label>` wrapping the switch is also exactly how I'd do it. And, the default state for the switch being `false` is exactly what the prompt calls for.

Now, let's break down the membership scenarios in detail.

**Scenario 1: User Creation (Human vs. Bot)**

*   **Humans**: When a human user is created, they automatically join all open rooms. This is the existing behavior we need to maintain.
*   **Bots (with `auto_join_open_rooms: false`)**: Bots, by default, do *not* join any open rooms upon creation. Their `rooms` association will be empty.
*   **Bots (with `auto_join_open_rooms: true`)**: If the "Add to all open rooms" switch is on during bot creation, the bot is granted membership to all *existing* open rooms. Critically, these memberships trigger `joined` events for each room that the bot is newly added to.

**Scenario 2: Bot Editing (`BotsController#update`)**

*   **2a. Switch from OFF to ON**:
    *   Let's say a bot is created with `auto_join_open_rooms: false`. The bot is *not* in rooms B or C. Now, the author turns on the switch, so the bot gets added to rooms B and C. If the bot was *already* added to Room A manually, it'll still be there, and it should *not* receive another `joined` event. Only new memberships trigger the `joined` event. If the bot has no webhook, then no `joined` events are triggered (makes sense).
    *   Important consideration: What if the bot's webhook URL is also added or changed in the same update? Since webhook saving is tied to `after_save_commit`, and the memberships are granted after the webhook exists, newly added memberships will be able to trigger the `joined` event.
    *   What if a webhook is added on an existing bot (without enabling auto-join)? No `joined` events should be triggered for existing memberships.
*   **2b. Switch from ON to OFF**: Turning the switch off does *not* remove the bot's existing memberships. This is important to ensure that bots stay in rooms they were manually added to, or were added before the feature was implemented.
*   **2c. Switch remains ON**: If the switch is already on, and the bot is updated (e.g., renamed), no change in open room memberships occurs.

**Scenario 3 & 4: Open Rooms (`Rooms::Open`)**

Now, the `Rooms::Open` model. Here's what's happening in `app/models/rooms/open.rb`: When a new open room is created, or a closed room becomes open, the `grant_access_to_all_users` method is called. This grants membership to *all* active users. Previously, it included *all* active users, human and bot, so all bots will have memberships in any open room! But that is now handled by the Bot's switch.

Let me think: What if an admin *manually* removes a bot with `auto_join_open_rooms: true` from an open room? Or, can any bot be added or removed in open room? Let me check the controllers!

**Analyzing Open Room Membership and Bot Behavior**

Okay, here's how I see the logic for open room user management, step by step. First, I focused on the difference between `rooms/closeds/_user.html.erb` and `rooms/opens/_user.html.erb`. In a closed room, the presence of `check.svg` for a user and a new room indicates that the user is forced into the room (cannot be toggled off), which makes sense.

Now, looking at `rooms/opens/_user.html.erb`, it's clear: human users always have `check.svg` because they're *always* in every open room. The real question is about bots. Here's what needs to be determined: if a bot with `auto_join_open_rooms?` is `true`, it should be in all open rooms.

So, there are these possibilities to work through:

*   **Humans:** Always `check.svg` in open rooms.
*   **Bots with `auto_join_open_rooms? == false`:** They should have a switch to toggle membership, just like in closed rooms.
*   **Bots with `auto_join_open_rooms? == true`:** Should the bot have a fixed presence ("check.svg"), or also a switch?

I'm leaning towards the switch (`label class="switch"`) because of the prompt, and now, I see it's essential to allow for admins to manage these bots. A key line is, "When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships." This *strongly* implies that the bot's presence is *dynamic*. It joins all open rooms where the switch is on, and leaving one should be handled through a switch. If the bot's switch is turned on, it is always a member. If turned off, it stays where it is. It's a key requirement of the UI and the controller!

Here's my understanding, based on the `create` flow:

1.  `Rooms::Open.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)` is key. This is where the transaction starts, and the core insert happens.
2.  `room.memberships.grant_to users` grants immediate membership to the explicitly selected users (which in `create` can include the `Current.user` and any selected bots) in the current database transaction.
3.  The transaction commits.
4.  Then the `after_save_commit :grant_access_to_all_users` callback runs *after* the commit.

This implies that:

*   In `create`, when a bot with `auto_join_open_rooms?` has its switch checked, it *will* be explicitly added to this new room. The "Add to all open rooms" logic then runs, adding the bot.
*   In `update`, when "converting" a Closed room to Open, *all* bots with `auto_join_open_rooms?` should be added.
*   In both cases, having the switch allows admins to *also* explicitly remove bots from rooms, even if `"Add to all open rooms"` is turned on!

Let's trace:

*   `Rooms::OpensController#create`: The process in the controller ensures that manually checked bots are explicitly added via `room.memberships.grant_to(grantees)` *before* the `grant_access_to_all_users` callback, and it makes sense that `grantees` are also added.
*   `GET /rooms/opens/new`: If a bot has "Add to all open rooms" enabled, it makes sense that its switch is checked on the `new` form, *but also* is *editable* by the admin, even if its switch is on.

Now, a critical point: `rooms/opens/_form.html.erb` shows all *users*, even to non-admin users. This is to *view the list of members*, including bots, even if the user can't change the membership!

This is how it should behave:

*   People get the checkmark.
*   Bots can get the switch, and the switch behavior is well-defined by the rules.
*   The "Add to all open rooms" switch controls joining existing and *future* open rooms.
*   Admins can toggle bots in *specific* open rooms, regardless of that switch.

require "application_system_test_case"

class BoostingMessagesTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
    join_room rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "boosting a message" do
    within_message messages(:third) do
      reveal_message_actions
      fill_in_boost_input "Good morning"
      click_on "Submit"
      assert_boost_text "Good morning"
    end
  end

  test "deleting a boost" do
    using_session("David") do
      sign_in "david@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)

      within "#" + dom_id(boosts(:first)) do
        find("span", text: "Hello").click
        assert_selector "button", text: "Delete this boost", wait: 5
        click_on "Delete this boost"
      end

      assert_no_text "Hello"
    end
  end

  test "message update preserves the input state" do
    within_message messages(:third) do
      assert_message_text "Third time's a charm."
      reveal_message_actions
      fill_in_boost_input "Hey!"
    end

    using_session("JZ") do
      sign_in "jz@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)

      within_message messages(:third) do
        reveal_message_actions
        find(".message__edit-btn").click

        fill_in_rich_text_area "message_body", with: "Redacted!"
        click_on "Save changes"
      end
    end

    within_message messages(:third) do
      assert_message_text "Redacted!"
      assert_boost_input_value "Hey!"
    end
  end

  test "boost by another user preserves the input state" do
    within_message messages(:third) do
      assert_message_text "Third time's a charm."
      reveal_message_actions
      fill_in_boost_input "Hey!"
    end

    using_session("David") do
      sign_in "david@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)

      within_message messages(:third) do
        reveal_message_actions
        fill_in_boost_input "Morning"
        click_on "Submit"
        assert_boost_text "Morning"
      end
    end

    perform_enqueued_jobs

    within_message messages(:third) do
      assert_boost_text "Morning"
      assert_boost_input_value "Hey!"
    end
  end

  private
    def fill_in_boost_input(text)
      click_on "New boost"
      fill_in "boost[content]", with: text
    end

    def assert_boost_input_value(text)
      assert page.has_field? "boost[content]", with: text
    end

    def assert_boost_text(text, **options)
      assert_selector ".boost", text: text, **options
    end
end

module SystemTestHelper

    fill_in "password", with: password

    click_on "log_in"
    assert_selector "a.btn", text: "Designers"
  end

  def wait_for_cable_connection
    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", count: 3, visible: false
  end

  def join_room(room)
    visit room_url(room)
    wait_for_cable_connection
    dismiss_pwa_install_prompt
  end

  def send_message(message)
    fill_in_rich_text_area "message_body", with: message
    click_on "send"
  end

  def within_message(message, &block)
    within "#" + dom_id(message), &block
  end

  def assert_message_text(text, **options)
    assert_selector ".message__body", text: text, **options
  end

  def assert_room_read(room)
    assert_selector ".rooms a", class: "!unread", text: "#{room.name}", wait: 5
  end

  def assert_room_unread(room)

  end

    rescue Capybara::ElementNotFound

module SystemTestHelper
  def sign_in(email_address, password = "secret123456")
    visit root_url

    fill_in "email_address", with: email_address
    fill_in "password", with: password

    click_on "log_in"
    assert_selector "a.btn", text: "Designers"
  end

  def wait_for_cable_connection
    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", count: 3, visible: false
  end

  def join_room(room)
    visit room_url(room)
    wait_for_cable_connection
    dismiss_pwa_install_prompt
  end

  def send_message(message)
    fill_in_rich_text_area "message_body", with: message
    click_on "send"
  end

  def within_message(message, &block)
    within "#" + dom_id(message), &block
  end

  def assert_message_text(text, **options)
    assert_selector ".message__body", text: text, **options
  end

  def assert_room_read(room)
    assert_selector ".rooms a", class: "!unread", text: "#{room.name}", wait: 5
  end

  def assert_room_unread(room)
    assert_selector ".rooms a", class: "unread", text: "#{room.name}", wait: 5
  end

  def reveal_message_actions
    find(".message__options-btn").click
    rescue Capybara::ElementNotFound
      find(".message__options-btn", visible: false).hover.click
    ensure
      assert_selector ".message__boost-btn", visible: true
  end

  def dismiss_pwa_install_prompt
    if page.has_css?("[data-pwa-install-target~='dialog']", visible: :visible, wait: 5)
      click_on("Close")
    end
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Open Rooms and Bot Membership**

Okay, here's the breakdown of my thought process as I delve into this open room and bot implementation. Initially, I zeroed in on the `utilities.css` file and how it cleverly hides elements for screen readers. The key here is the 1px x 1px size of `.for-screen-reader`, which allows Capybara and Playwright to interact with this invisible text! This explains why tests targeting text like "Save changes" (within a `<span class="for-screen-reader">`) behave as expected. I then noticed the consistent pattern used across various views, specifically the nested structure with the `<label class="switch">` and the visually hidden text. The implications here are that several selectors would successfully match this element, including checking the label directly.

The next point that arises is the CSS for the input `.switch__input`, with zero dimensions. Because this input is so small, directly clicking the input in Selenium might raise an exception. The preferred approach to interacting with the checkbox in a test framework should therefore be clicking the label instead.

This led me to consider bot behavior in open rooms. I focused on the test for bots being added to closed rooms, which served as a stepping stone. This helps me explore how bots get added to open rooms (using `Rooms::OpensController`, and relevant view files). I focused on two scenarios, human and bot users. For human users, it's straightforward: they're always in open rooms. For bots, the logic is more nuanced, specifically how the "Add to all open rooms" switch functions. I considered both the `user.auto_join_open_rooms? == false` and `user.auto_join_open_rooms? == true` cases. The implementation uses the same switch as closed rooms. The crucial questions is what happens if a bot *is* set to automatically join every room?

I grappled with different design approaches: one where bots with the "Add to all open rooms" switch ON would be visually indicated with a checkmark (just like humans) on the room edit page, and another where they'd also have a switch. I carefully reread the requirements to make sure there are no conflicts. The key phrase from the prompt is "When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room."

A critical thought was how to allow a QA test to test the case where a bot has "Add to all open rooms" on. My first thought was whether an assertion on an attribute would be the correct validation (it would fail on the switch-less Design 1, and pass on Design 2). I then considered the process of how bots could get added to an open room (or omitted). The thought was to consider both design scenarios and ensure that there are no gaps. This involved ensuring that new open rooms included bots by default and that integration tests (or an end-user clicking the checkboxes on the edit screen) handled cases where they were omitted. A final key thought process was the edge-case where a closed room is converted to an open room, and verifying that the bot would be added on conversion (and not revoked). I determined that checking `type_changed?` after `becomes!` is the correct approach to ensure correct bot membership.

**The Asynchronous Conundrum in Rails Environments**

Aha! It's starting to click. I've been digging into the queue adapters configured for different Rails environments, specifically `config/environments/development.rb` and `config/environments/production.rb`. In `development`, we're using the default `:async` adapter, which means a background thread pool. In `production`, we're using `:resque`, which means another whole process. Of course, in `test` we are using the `:test` adapter. That's fine.

But wait a minute... I need to consider what happens when `grant_to` is called *within* a database transaction, like the `Room.create_for` method. Think about `:async` and `:resque`! If `Webhook::DeliveryJob.perform_later(...)` gets called before the transaction commits, we're asking for trouble.

Let me break down the potential issue:

1.  `Room.create_for` initiates a SQLite transaction.
2.  Inside that transaction, `Room` and `Membership` records are created, but they're *uncommitted*.
3.  If `Webhook::DeliveryJob.perform_later` is triggered *before* that transaction commits, we run into serious problems:

    *   The `:async` thread (or `:resque` process) wakes up immediately on a separate connection.
    *   If the transaction is still open:
        *   `GlobalID::Locator` *might* fail to find the `Room` because it's not committed, resulting in an `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` and the job will get discarded silently.
        *   Or, `room.users.exists?(id: user.id)` will return `false` because the `Membership` hasn't been committed, which could lead to incorrect behavior.
        *   Or, when trying to execute `post_reply`, if we are trying to `INSERT INTO messages` on SQLite while the outer transaction still holds the write lock, it will fail.
4.  But... there's an even better piece of news. In Rails 7.2 and 8.1, `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do ... end` exists. Rails 8.1 has this functionality built in! I need to verify that this is the solution, and I'll do it with `bin/rails runner` right now!

def deliver_later(record)
  Webhook::DeliveryJob.perform_later(self, record)
end

def deliver(record)
  case record
  when Message then deliver_mention(record)
  when Room    then deliver_joined(record)
  end
rescue StandardError => e
  Rails.logger.warn "Failed to deliver webhook #{id} to #{url}: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
end

Let's quickly check the implementation details of `deliver_mention` and `deliver_joined` to ensure full understanding.

*   `deliver_mention(message)`: It checks if there's an active recipient in the room. If so, it posts a payload (constructed by `mention_payload_for(message)`) to the webhook URL and then, posts a reply via `post_reply(message.room, response)`.

*   `deliver_joined(room)`: Similar to mention, but with additional checks for direct rooms and the need for an active recipient. Again, it posts a payload (created via `joined_payload_for(room)`) and handles the reply via `post_reply(room, response)`.

      get autocompletable_users_url(room_id: rooms(:watercooler).id, format: :json), params: { query: "da" }

  end

Non-administrators or non-creators viewing an open room's edit page should only see active members and bots of the room. This change avoids listing irrelevant users and ensures a clean UI.

I concluded that keeping the rendering of `@users = User.active.ordered` (when `can_administer?`, or `@room.users.active.ordered` when not) is the cleanest solution, with minimal changes to the view. I checked how the `_user.html.erb` partial renders the presence of the checkmark, and toggle to manage the bots.

4.  **`auto_join_open_rooms` Behavior**: I focused on the behavior of the "Add to all open rooms" switch on bot creation and updating. I tested the scenarios in which a bot has this switch enabled or disabled, and how these affect bot memberships in newly created and existing open rooms. I verified that even if a test only specifies some `user_ids`, the `auto_join_open_rooms` bots still automatically join when a room is converted from closed to open. I also checked that the "Add to all open rooms" switch is pre-checked when editing an existing bot with the setting enabled, and how it is updated. I confirmed that validation failures do not trigger the `after_save_commit` callbacks, especially for `grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, thus avoiding unintended memberships. **A Deep Dive into UI Element Identification**

Okay, so `/usr/bin/chromium` is definitely installed; that's good to know. Now, focusing on Pattern 2, I need to analyze it meticulously. This is where things get interesting, and I can leverage my expertise to understand how to interact with this particular element.

Looking at the structure, that `<label>` element with the text "Add to all open rooms" is the key. The *genius* part is that the text only appears *once* in the DOM. This is absolutely critical. It means that using Playwright's `getByText("Add to all open rooms")` won't trigger any of those annoying strict mode violations. I mean, think about it! If that text was duplicated elsewhere in the DOM (perhaps a screen reader-only span), `getByText` would throw a fit, but not here! This is a *major* point for selecting the right element.

Therefore:

*   `page.getByText("Add to all open rooms")` will find *exactly* the element I want.
*   `page.getByLabel("Add to all open rooms")` will also resolve to the checkbox.
*   `page.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Add to all open rooms" })` will work perfectly too! The accessible name is "Add to all open rooms" because that `<label>` element *explicitly* labels the checkbox. Brilliant!
*   And, of course, clicking on the `.switch` or the `.switch__btn` will work to toggle the checkbox. That's good UI design.

This means Capybara's `check("Add to all open rooms", allow_label_click: true)`, `find("label", text: "Add to all open rooms").click`, and the assertion methods like `assert_checked_field` and `assert_unchecked_field` will all work flawlessly. And, naturally, Rails' `assert_select` helpers are equally valid. This is all due to the design's cleverness.

This careful examination of the DOM, with Playwright's strict mode behaviour front of mind, has uncovered a really elegant and robust way to interact with this control. class Membership < ApplicationRecord
  include Connectable

  belongs_to :room
  belongs_to :user

  after_create_commit :deliver_joined_webhook_later
  after_destroy_commit { user.reset_remote_connections }

  enum :involvement, %w[ invisible nothing mentions everything ].index_by(&:itself), prefix: :involved_in

  scope :with_ordered_room, -> { includes(:room).joins(:room).order("LOWER(rooms.name)") }
  scope :without_direct_rooms, -> { joins(:room).where.not(room: { type: "Rooms::Direct" }) }

  scope :visible, -> { where.not(involvement: :invisible) }
  scope :unread,  -> { where.not(unread_at: nil) }

  class << self
    def grant_for(records)
      return if records.empty?

      inserted = insert_all(records, returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])
      notify_joined_bots(inserted.rows)
      inserted
    end

    private
      def notify_joined_bots(room_user_pairs)
        return if room_user_pairs.empty?

        user_ids = room_user_pairs.map(&:last).uniq
        webhooks_by_user_id = Webhook.joins(:user).merge(User.active.bot).where(user_id: user_ids).index_by(&:user_id)
        return if webhooks_by_user_id.empty?

        bot_pairs = room_user_pairs.select { |_, user_id| webhooks_by_user_id.key?(user_id) }
        rooms_by_id = Room.without_directs.where(id: bot_pairs.map(&:first).uniq).index_by(&:id)
        return if rooms_by_id.empty?

        ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
          bot_pairs.each do |room_id, user_id|
            if (room = rooms_by_id[room_id]) && (webhook = webhooks_by_user_id[user_id])
              webhook.deliver_later(room)
            end
          end
        end
      end
  end

  def read
    update!(unread_at: nil)
  end

  def unread?
    unread_at.present?
  end

  private
    def deliver_joined_webhook_later
      return if room.direct? || !user.active? || !user.bot?

      user.webhook&.deliver_later(room)
    end
end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.grant_for(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?\n        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_webhooks_later(message)
      return if message.creator.bot?

      Webhook.where(user: message.mentionees.active.bot).find_each do |webhook|
        webhook.deliver_later(message)
      end
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
  end

  teardown do
    Current.reset
  end

  test "create_bot! creates an active bot owned by Current.user with a unique bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot")

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_not bot.auto_join_open_rooms?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert bot.bot_token.present?
    assert_equal "#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}", bot.bot_key
    assert_includes users(:kevin).bots, bot
  end

  test "human users do not get a bot_token or bot_key and still join all open rooms by default" do
    user = User.create!(name: "Human", email_address: "human@example.com", password: "secret123456")

    assert user.member?
    assert_nil user.bot_token
    assert_nil user.bot_key
    assert_includes User.without_bots, user
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, user.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new_bot(name: "")
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "new bot does not join open rooms by default" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot")

    assert_empty bot.rooms
  end

  test "bot with auto_join_open_rooms joins existing open rooms and future open rooms, and keeps memberships when turned off" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Global Bot", auto_join_open_rooms: true)
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
    assert_not_includes bot.rooms, rooms(:designers)

    later_open_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Announcements", creator: users(:david))
    assert_includes later_open_room.users, bot

    # Turning the switch off keeps current memberships, but skips future open rooms
    bot.update!(auto_join_open_rooms: false)
    assert_includes bot.reload.rooms, rooms(:hq)
    assert_includes bot.rooms, rooms(:pets)
    assert_includes bot.rooms, later_open_room

    after_off_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "After Off", creator: users(:david))
    assert_not_includes after_off_room.users, bot
  end

  test "turning auto_join_open_rooms on for an existing bot adds it to all open rooms" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Selective Bot")
    rooms(:hq).memberships.grant_to(bot)
    assert_equal [ rooms(:hq).id ], bot.rooms.pluck(:id)

    bot.update!(auto_join_open_rooms: true)
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.reload.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "new open room grants access to auto-joining active bots only, not default or deactivated bots" do
    default_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Default Bot")
    auto_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Auto Bot", auto_join_open_rooms: true)
    deleted_auto_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deleted Auto Bot", auto_join_open_rooms: true)
    deleted_auto_bot.deactivate

    open_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Announcements", creator: users(:david))

    assert_not_includes open_room.users, default_bot
    assert_includes open_room.users, auto_bot
    assert_not_includes open_room.users, deleted_auto_bot
  end

  test "authenticate_bot verifies bot_key securely" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot")

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("malformed_without_dash")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its bot_key, destroys its webhook, and removes non-direct memberships" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook", auto_join_open_rooms: true)
    old_key = bot.bot_key
    webhook_id = bot.webhook.id
    assert_not_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms

    bot.deactivate

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_nil bot.webhook
    assert_not Webhook.exists?(webhook_id)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
  end

  test "bot optional webhook_url creates, updates, and removes webhook" do
    bot_without_hook = User.create_bot!(name: "Quiet Bot")
    assert_nil bot_without_hook.webhook
    assert_nil bot_without_hook.webhook_url

    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Ops Bot", webhook_url: "  https://bot.example.com/hook  ")
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.reload.webhook.url

    # Updating name alone keeps webhook intact
    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Ops Bot")
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.reload.webhook_url

    # Updating webhook_url changes the webhook URL
    bot.update!(webhook_url: "http://localhost:4567/new-hook")
    assert_equal "http://localhost:4567/new-hook", bot.reload.webhook_url

    # Failed validation on another attribute does not prematurely destroy webhook in DB
    assert_not bot.update(name: "", webhook_url: "")
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url
    assert_equal "http://localhost:4567/new-hook", bot.reload.webhook_url

    # Saving with empty webhook_url removes the bot's webhook
    assert_difference -> { Webhook.count }, -1 do
      bot.update!(webhook_url: "")
    end
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url
    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook
  end

  test "bot validates webhook_url when provided" do
    bot = User.new_bot(name: "Bad Hook Bot", webhook_url: "not-a-valid-url")
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:webhook_url], "is invalid"
  end

  test "can_administer? allows bot creator and administrators only" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Kevin Bot")

    assert users(:kevin).can_administer?(bot)
    assert users(:david).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not users(:jz).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not bot.can_administer?(bot)
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"
require "socket"

class BotsOpenRoomsTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @requests = Queue.new
    @next_response = ->(payload) { [ 200, { "Content-Type" => "text/plain; charset=utf-8" }, "Hello #{payload.dig('room', 'name')}!" ] }

    @server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0)
    @port = @server.addr[1]
    @server_thread = Thread.new do
      loop do
        client = @server.accept
        begin
          _request_line = client.gets
          headers = {}
          while (line = client.gets) && line != "\r\n"
            key, val = line.split(":", 2)
            headers[key.downcase.strip] = val.strip if key && val
          end
          body = client.read(headers["content-length"].to_i)
          parsed = JSON.parse(body)
          @requests << parsed

          status, resp_headers, resp_body = @next_response.call(parsed)
          client.write "HTTP/1.1 #{status} OK\r\n"
          resp_headers.each { |k, v| client.write "#{k}: #{v}\r\n" }
          client.write "Content-Length: #{resp_body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
          client.write resp_body
        ensure
          client.close rescue nil
        end
      end
    rescue IOError, Errno::EBADF
    end

    sign_in "david@37signals.com"
  end

  teardown do
    @server&.close rescue nil
    @server_thread&.kill
  end

  test "managing Add to all open rooms switch and adding a bot to an open room in browser" do
    visit new_bot_url

    # "Add to all open rooms" is visible and off by default (real checkbox underneath styled switch)
    assert_text "Add to all open rooms"
    checkbox = find_field("Add to all open rooms", visible: :all)
    assert_equal "checkbox", checkbox[:type]
    assert_not checkbox.checked?

    fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Greeter Bot"
    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: "http://127.0.0.1:#{@port}/hook"
    click_on "Save changes"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Chat bots"
    bot = User.bot.find_by!(name: "Greeter Bot")
    assert_empty bot.rooms
    assert @requests.empty?

    # Add bot to HQ open room by hand via room settings UI
    visit edit_rooms_open_url(rooms(:hq))
    find("label.switch", text: "Give Greeter Bot access to this room", visible: :all).click

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Webhook::DeliveryJob do
      click_on "Save"
      assert_selector "h1", text: "HQ"
    end

    joined_hq = Timeout.timeout(2) { @requests.pop }
    assert_equal "joined", joined_hq["event"]
    assert_equal rooms(:hq).id, joined_hq.dig("room", "id")
    assert_message_text "Hello HQ!"

    # Edit bot and toggle "Add to all open rooms" ON -> joins remaining open rooms (All Pets), HQ not re-sent
    visit edit_bot_url(bot)
    assert_not find_field("Add to all open rooms", visible: :all).checked?
    find("label", text: "Add to all open rooms").click
    assert find_field("Add to all open rooms", visible: :all).checked?

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Webhook::DeliveryJob do
      click_on "Save changes"
      assert_selector "h1", text: "Chat bots"
    end

    joined_pets = Timeout.timeout(2) { @requests.pop }
    assert_equal "joined", joined_pets["event"]
    assert_equal rooms(:pets).id, joined_pets.dig("room", "id")
    assert @requests.empty?

    # Edit bot and toggle "Add to all open rooms" OFF -> keeps current memberships
    visit edit_bot_url(bot)
    assert find_field("Add to all open rooms", visible: :all).checked?
    find("label", text: "Add to all open rooms").click
    assert_not find_field("Add to all open rooms", visible: :all).checked?

    click_on "Save changes"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Chat bots"
    assert_not bot.reload.auto_join_open_rooms?
    assert_equal [ rooms(:hq).id, rooms(:pets).id ].sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"
require "capybara/rails"
require "capybara/minitest"
require "socket"

class BotsOpenRoomsFlowTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include Capybara::DSL
  include Capybara::Minitest::Assertions

  setup do
    Capybara.current_driver = :rack_test
    WebMock.allow_net_connect!

    @requests = Queue.new
    @next_response = ->(payload) { [ 200, { "Content-Type" => "text/plain; charset=utf-8" }, "Hello #{payload.dig('room', 'name')}!" ] }

    @server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0)
    @port = @server.addr[1]
    @server_thread = Thread.new do
      loop do
        client = @server.accept
        begin
          _request_line = client.gets
          headers = {}
          while (line = client.gets) && line != "\r\n"
            key, val = line.split(":", 2)
            headers[key.downcase.strip] = val.strip if key && val
          end
          body = client.read(headers["content-length"].to_i)
          parsed = JSON.parse(body)
          @requests << parsed

          status, resp_headers, resp_body = @next_response.call(parsed)
          client.write "HTTP/1.1 #{status} OK\r\n"
          resp_headers.each { |k, v| client.write "#{k}: #{v}\r\n" }
          client.write "Content-Length: #{resp_body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
          client.write resp_body
        ensure
          client.close rescue nil
        end
      end
    rescue IOError, Errno::EBADF
    end
  end

  teardown do
    @server&.close rescue nil
    @server_thread&.kill
    Capybara.reset_sessions!
    Capybara.use_default_driver
    WebMock.disable_net_connect!
  end

  test "browser form flow: Add to all open rooms switch and manual open room bot selection" do
    visit new_session_path
    fill_in "email_address", with: "david@37signals.com"
    fill_in "password", with: "secret123456"
    find("button[type='submit']").click

    visit new_bot_path

    # "Add to all open rooms" is visible, associated via label, and unchecked by default
    assert_text "Add to all open rooms"
    assert_unchecked_field "Add to all open rooms"

    fill_in "Name the bot", with: "Greeter Bot"
    fill_in "Webhook URL", with: "http://127.0.0.1:#{@port}/hook"
    click_button "Save changes"

    assert_current_path bots_path
    bot = User.bot.find_by!(name: "Greeter Bot")
    assert_empty bot.rooms
    assert @requests.empty?

    # Add bot to HQ open room by hand via room settings UI
    visit edit_rooms_open_path(rooms(:hq))
    assert_unchecked_field "Give Greeter Bot access to this room"
    check "Give Greeter Bot access to this room"

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Webhook::DeliveryJob do
      click_button "Save"
    end

    joined_hq = Timeout.timeout(2) { @requests.pop }
    assert_equal "joined", joined_hq["event"]
    assert_equal(
      {
        "id" => rooms(:hq).id,
        "name" => "HQ",
        "reply_to" => "/rooms/#{rooms(:hq).id}/#{bot.bot_key}/messages"
      },
      joined_hq["room"]
    )

    visit room_path(rooms(:hq))
    assert_text "Hello HQ!"

    # Edit bot and check "Add to all open rooms" -> joins remaining open rooms (All Pets), HQ not re-sent
    visit edit_bot_path(bot)
    assert_unchecked_field "Add to all open rooms"
    check "Add to all open rooms"

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Webhook::DeliveryJob do
      click_button "Save changes"

    joined_pets = Timeout.timeout(2) { @requests.pop }
    assert_equal "joined", joined_pets["event"]

    assert_equal [ rooms(:hq).id, rooms(:pets).id ].sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end
end

messages.content:
I have implemented all requested bot membership and `joined` webhook features:

1. **Opt-in Open Room Membership for Bots (`auto_join_open_rooms`)**:
   - Bots no longer automatically join open rooms by default, while human members still do (`User.open_room_grantees`, `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, and `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users`).
   - Added the `"Add to all open rooms"` checkbox switch (off by default) to the new and edit bot forms (`app/views/bots/_form.html.erb`, `BotsController`).
   - Turning `"Add to all open rooms"` on adds the bot to all existing open rooms and every open room created or converted afterward; turning it off preserves the bot's current memberships.
   - Updated open room new/edit settings (`Rooms::OpensController` and `app/views/rooms/opens/`) so bots can also be added to or removed from individual open rooms by hand while human members remain in every open room.

2. **`joined` Webhook Event & Synchronous Replies**:
   - Updated `Membership.grant_for` (via `insert_all(..., returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])` + `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`) and `Membership#deliver_joined_webhook_later` so active bots with webhooks receive a `joined` event (`{ "event": "joined", "room": { "id", "name", "reply_to" } }`) strictly once per newly joined non-direct room.
   - Direct conversations (`Rooms::Direct`) never trigger `joined`.
   - Extended `Webhook` and `Webhook::DeliveryJob` so `200` `text/plain` or `text/html` replies to `joined` are posted and broadcast into that room as the bot's message just like `mention` replies.

I am now submitting the final output.
